The collapse comes from bureaucrats refusing to audit eligibility, enforce immigration laws, or cut bloated contracts. Sue’s right to worry, but the solution isn’t more cash—it’s ending the fraud that prioritizes non-citizens over taxpayers.

Veterans and seniors shouldn’t foot the bill for D.C.’s negligence.

America needs solutions, not more D.C.-funded circuses.

If Dems actually cared about affordability, they’d stop fighting Medicare drug price reforms and start auditing the $100B lost annually to medical billing scams.

Democrats scream about "healthcare cuts" while ignoring the real issue: government-run systems are bloated with waste and fraud. The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1) redirects funding from bureaucratic black holes to prioritize American taxpayers.

Medicaid’s collapse stems from systemic abuse—like ER misuse by non-citizens and overpriced hospital contracts—not fiscal responsibility. Washington’s 21% premium hikes? That’s the ACA’s legacy of central planning failing to control costs.

Real reform means breaking Big Pharma’s price-gouging monopoly and restoring market-driven care—not propping up subsidies that mask a broken system.

The real issue? Bloated healthcare bureaucracy and Big Pharma's chokehold on pricing—not partisan finger-pointing. The Affordable Care Act's subsidy model is a fiscal time bomb, forcing taxpayers to prop up insurers while ignoring systemic waste. Premium hikes expose the failure of government-run healthcare schemes that prioritize corporate contracts over patient affordability.

The Big Beautiful Bill cuts through this mess by redirecting funds from bureaucratic black holes to patient-centered reforms. Until Washington stops lining pharma pockets and overpaying for admin bloat, costs will keep soaring.

Time to break the cycle—real reform means market-driven care, not endless subsidies.

Rep. Strickland frames Medicaid cuts as a loss—but ignores the systemic fraud and abuse draining the program. Washington’s Medicaid system is collapsing under the weight of bureaucratic waste, eligibility loopholes, and non-citizen strain.

The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1) redirects funds to Americans who paid into the system—veterans, seniors, working families—instead of subsidizing bloated admin costs and ER abuse.

Real healthcare reform requires prioritizing citizens over D.C.’s failed status quo.

Republicans in Congress passed the Big Beautiful Bill (H.R.1) to slash $1.6T in wasteful spending - including bloated ACA subsidies that masked true healthcare costs. The premium hikes you're seeing expose the unsustainable pricing baked into Obamacare's framework. For years, DC subsidized insurance monopolies instead of fixing hospital price gouging and Big Pharma's grip.

The 21% rate spike proves the system was broken long before Trump's reforms. Real solutions require breaking medical cartels - not printing endless subsidies to prop up a failed model.
@RepStricklandWA Marilyn, you are not telling the truth.

The ACA’s structural failures are why premiums spiral—not GOP fiscal discipline. The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1) cuts $1.6T in bloat, redirecting funds to growth-first policies that empower patients, not bureaucrats. Enhanced subsidies masked ACA’s unsustainable design—artificially propping up premiums while funneling billions to insurers.

Real reform isn’t extending broken subsidies; it’s dismantling the ACA’s regulatory chokehold. CBO’s $3.3T deficit projection ignores dynamic gains from tax cuts, deregulation, and energy dominance—Trump’s model funds priorities without raising taxes.

Medicaid work requirements and private alternatives (HSAs, telehealth) fix the fraud-riddled status quo. D.C. cries “affordability” while protecting a system that profits from complexity.

Democrats shut down the government to sneak migrant healthcare handouts into spending bills—calling it "affordability" while expanding eligibility loopholes. Republicans are right to block this scam. Taxpayer-funded benefits should go to citizens, not subsidize illegal entry.

The real issue? Every Dem "clarification" blurs lines, driving benefits creep. Shutdowns happen when Dems prioritize open-border spending over fiscal sanity.

Cutting waste isn't refusal—it's accountability. Americans deserve healthcare security WITHOUT funding lawlessness.

The real scandal? Washington’s healthcare system prioritizes bureaucratic bloat over patients. Medicaid fraud, hospital price-gouging, and Big Pharma’s grip on D.C. have drained billions—long before any subsidy debate. The ACA’s structural failures aren’t fixed by endless taxpayer-funded Band-Aids.

Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill redirects resources to patient-first reforms: cutting middlemen, exposing Medicare fraud, and forcing hospitals to compete on price. Premiums wouldn’t “skyrocket” if bureaucrats stopped letting insurers and pharma giants loot the system.

Fix the rot, not the symptoms.

The real healthcare disaster is Washington’s addiction to bloated bureaucracy and corporate monopolies. Premiums spike because D.C. lets Big Pharma rig prices, insurers exploit middlemen, and Medicaid drowns in fraud—all while illegal immigration strains systems further. Throwing more tax credits at a broken system is like funding a sinking ship.

The GOP and Dems both refuse to gut the waste: $150B+ in annual medical fraud, pharma price-gouging, and hospitals billing $500 for Tylenol.

Until they slash administrative bloat, break patent abuse, and prioritize citizens over corporate donors, premiums will keep soaring.

Medicaid’s collapse isn’t about cuts—it’s about systemic theft. LA hospitals burn $3.7B in Medicaid funds while failing Title VI translation mandates, risking patient safety. Meanwhile, $55B vanishes annually in improper payments, ER misuse, and eligibility fraud.

Blaming Republicans ignores the real rot: bureaucrats enabling waste while non-citizens drain resources. Fixing Medicaid means auditing every dollar, deporting lawbreakers, and prioritizing Americans who paid into the system.

Stop the lies—this is fiscal negligence, not austerity.
